title: P1c: progressive memory recall that stops when sufficient (local notes, bus evidence, claude-mem, graph) with every recall recorded as a run row in bucket memory; packets use the same bounded recall
spec:
Phase I P1 (brief .orchestrator/phase-i-program.md, section progressive memory recall: cheapest-first, stop when sufficient, never retrieve richer memory merely because it exists; P0 asks that memory recall be attributed where measurable). Base goal/T-0445 after P1b (T-0462) merges. Facts: the memory skill's recall lives in .claude/skills/memory/scripts/recall.py (layers: notes in .orchestrator/memory/*.md, bus results, claude-mem observations, graphify graph; ranking may use orchestrator.jev_rank); spawn.packet fills "matching gotchas" from the notes layer (spawn.py, gotcha match by path); no recall call writes a run row today (scout T-0446).
1. recall.py: a function recall(query, *, layers=("notes","bus","claude-mem","graph"), budget_hits=8, min_score=0.5, budget_chars=6000, task=None) that consults layers in that order and stops as soon as hits >= budget_hits with score >= min_score or the char budget is spent; returns {hits: [...], layers_consulted: [...], stopped_at: <layer or None>, chars: int}. The CLI subcommands (index, get) keep working; add `recall.py index --progressive` that uses the function and prints layers_consulted in the header. Unavailable layers (claude-mem down, no graph) are skipped and named in layers_consulted with "unavailable", never an error.
2. Recording: every recall() call with a task or goal id logs one row through bus.log_run with role "memory" (bucket memory via attribution), task, goal_id when known, layers_consulted, stopped_at, hits, chars, est_tokens = chars // 4, duration_s, usd absent. Rows without a task still log with role memory and bucket memory so the unknown group shows them.
3. spawn.packet and the P1b packets take their memory titles / matching gotchas through recall(query=<task title + scope paths>, layers=("notes","bus"), budget_hits=5, task=task id): notes and bus only for packets (the two cheapest layers), so packet building never touches claude-mem or the graph; the packet section names layers_consulted in its header sources.
4. pool.toml [memory] table with the defaults (budget_hits, min_score, budget_chars, packet_layers) and comments; README one paragraph under Memory.
Tests tests/test_memory_skill.py: test_recall_stops_after_budget_hits_in_notes_layer (bus and later layers never called: monkeypatch counters), test_recall_skips_unavailable_layer_and_names_it, test_recall_logs_memory_run_row_with_task_and_layers, test_recall_progressive_cli_header; tests/test_spawn.py: test_packet_memory_uses_notes_and_bus_only. Existing tests green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; commit with the task id including every named test; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: recall consults layers cheapest-first and stops at the budget; every recall with a task logs a run row with role memory; packets use notes and bus layers only; pool.toml [memory] documents the defaults
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
